provenance.userLayer: none supplied: gazetteer positions and unedited atlas features

coordinateSystem.name: Thalorien atlas world space
coordinateSystem.axes: x increases east, y increases south; north is up
coordinateSystem.scale: none: the campaign documents state no distances precise enough to fix one
coordinateSystem.note: One coordinate system is used by the gazetteer, the atlas geometry, both guide images and the finished artwork.

transform.note: Affine, axis-aligned, no rotation. Pixel (0, 0) is the top-left corner of the top-left pixel. Valid for any uniformly resized copy after dividing by the resize factor.

canonCategories.confirmed-canon: Stated in the four authorized campaign documents: that the place exists, its name, and the quoted relations between places.
canonCategories.atlas-interpretation: The atlas giving a confirmed fact a drawable form: every coordinate, outline, extent, river course and ridgeline. Not canon.
canonCategories.proposed-atlas-addition: Invented by the atlas for a coherent world; awaiting the Dungeon Master. Not canon, removable by the player.

statedRelations.quote: the Thornwall blossomed white along three leagues
a crescent moon in a well (Elendrath)
the Mask east to Dun Ommar
the Deep Anvil of Dun Ommar
three leagues north of the Toll-stone

terrainRegions.description: The ancient wood of Uchkeken. Drawn fire-scarred, because the documents speak of burnt stumps and burnt hills; its bounds are the atlas’s.
basisQuotes: among the burnt stumps beyond the White Tree
terrainRegions.edgeNote: Authored outline. The atlas draws the edge irregularly, within about 22 world units of this polygon.

terrainRegions.description: The Silverwood. Drawn as a great wood on the strength of its name alone; nothing is recorded of its extent.
terrainRegions.basisNote: Rests on the place name alone.
terrainRegions.edgeNote: Authored outline. The atlas draws the edge irregularly, within about 22 world units of this polygon.

terrainRegions.description: The Harrow: shepherds’ country with peat. Drawn as open heath.
terrainRegions.edgeNote: Authored outline. The atlas draws the edge irregularly, within about 22 world units of this polygon.

terrainRegions.description: The Sarnmoor, drawn as moorland on the strength of its name.
terrainRegions.basisNote: Rests on the place name alone.
terrainRegions.edgeNote: Authored outline. The atlas draws the edge irregularly, within about 22 world units of this polygon.

terrainRegions.name: The Alderwilds
terrainRegions.description: Wet alder and willow woodland between Harrowmere and the Willowford.
terrainRegions.relation: West of Harrowmere, east of the Willowford.
terrainRegions.edgeNote: Authored outline. The atlas draws the edge irregularly, within about 22 world units of this polygon.

terrainRegions.name: Eastmere Forest
terrainRegions.description: A broad lowland forest in the south-east, unvisited and unremarked in the record.
terrainRegions.edgeNote: Authored outline. The atlas draws the edge irregularly, within about 22 world units of this polygon.

terrainRegions.name: The Southing Wood
terrainRegions.description: Woodland south of the long hills. Proposed as the country a place called the Singing Glade might lie beside.
terrainRegions.relation: East of Ennor-Lûth, south of the long hills.
terrainRegions.edgeNote: Authored outline. The atlas draws the edge irregularly, within about 22 world units of this polygon.

ridgelines.description: The mountain of Kharûn, drawn as a massif. The documents give it a peak; the range around it is interpolation.
Western shoulder of the pass crossed on the way north from Harrowmere. Only the pass itself is recorded.
Eastern shoulder of the same pass.
The high fells of the north-east, beyond the Ironway, where Taur-Galen stands.
The long hills that lie between Uchkeken and Ennor-Lûth.

ridgelines.name: The Grey Shoulders
ridgelines.description: A lower western arm of the Kharûn heights, bare grey rock above the tree line.
ridgelines.relation: Runs west from the Kharûn massif.

ridgelines.name: The Anvil Heights
ridgelines.description: Steep heights behind Dun Ommar. Proposed as the rock a dwarf-hold with a thousand-step stair would be cut into.
ridgelines.relation: East of Dun Ommar, running north to south.

rivers.description: The river Nindor. Recorded: one goes north-east up it from the Grey Step to the Three Cairns. Its course below the Grey Step is the atlas’s guess.
basisQuotes: from the Grey Step, NE up the Nindor 4 days
rivers.courseNote: The smoothed, meandering course the atlas and both guides draw (world units, 3 decimals).

rivers.description: The Senn. Recorded: river-folk, a ford, and Aranthal’s river wards. That it runs from the northern spurs past Aranthal to the sea is interpolation.
rivers.courseNote: The smoothed, meandering course the atlas and both guides draw (world units, 3 decimals).

rivers.name: The Willowwater
rivers.description: The river crossed at the Willowford. A ford implies a river; its name and course are proposed.
rivers.relation: Flows south from the Grey Shoulders through the Willowford to the western sea.
rivers.courseNote: The smoothed, meandering course the atlas and both guides draw (world units, 3 decimals).

rivers.name: The Eastrun
rivers.description: A river draining the Anvil Heights southward through Eastmere Forest.
rivers.relation: Rises south of the Anvil Heights and leaves the map to the south.
rivers.courseNote: The smoothed, meandering course the atlas and both guides draw (world units, 3 decimals).

rivers.name: The Fell Beck
rivers.description: A cold stream out of Cairnwater that joins the Nindor.
rivers.relation: Tributary of the Nindor from the east.
rivers.courseNote: The smoothed, meandering course the atlas and both guides draw (world units, 3 decimals).

rivers.name: The Hill Brook
rivers.description: A brook off the long hills that joins the Senn above Aranthal.
rivers.relation: Tributary of the Senn from the south-east.
rivers.courseNote: The smoothed, meandering course the atlas and both guides draw (world units, 3 decimals).

lakes.description: A mere beside Harrowmere, drawn only because of the town’s name.
lakes.basisNote: Rests on the place name alone.

lakes.description: The tarn north of the Cinder Gorge.
basisQuotes: the tarn half a mile north

lakes.name: Cairnwater
lakes.description: A tarn under the northern fells.

roads.name: The Hillway
roads.description: An old drove-road along the northern foot of the long hills. No record mentions it.
roads.relation: From Aranthal east along the long hills toward Fallowsteading.

pointFeatures.name: Sennbridge
pointFeatures.description: An old stone bridge over the Senn. (The record has a Senn ford; this bridge is an addition, not that ford.)
pointFeatures.relation: On the Senn south-east of Harrowmere.

pointFeatures.name: The Three Sisters
pointFeatures.description: Three standing stones on a crest of the long hills, a waymark for travellers.
pointFeatures.relation: On the long hills, north of Ennor-Lûth.

pointFeatures.name: Fallowsteading
pointFeatures.description: A farmstead village on the open ground south of the Harrow.
pointFeatures.relation: South of the Harrow, north-west of Eastmere Forest.

recordedRoutes.label: The Moonroad
recordedRoutes.geometry: schematic: a line between the stops. The documents give no road geometry. Drawn live by the website, never part of the artwork.

recordedRoutes.label: The Ironway
recordedRoutes.quote: narrow gorge on the Ironway three leagues north of the Toll-stone
recordedRoutes.geometry: schematic: a line between the stops. The documents give no road geometry. Drawn live by the website, never part of the artwork.

recordedRoutes.label: Way to Taur-Galen
recordedRoutes.quote: from the Grey Step, NE up the Nindor 4 days; at the Three Cairns climb Hirnost
recordedRoutes.geometry: schematic: a line between the stops. The documents give no road geometry. Drawn live by the website, never part of the artwork.

terrainClasses.label: Open lowland
terrainClasses.paintAs: Open grassland, meadow and farmed valley floor.

terrainClasses.label: Scattered groves (texture only, not data)
terrainClasses.paintAs: Loose copses and hedgerow trees thinning into open country. Placement is free.

terrainClasses.label: Forest: the Silverwood
terrainClasses.paintAs: Dense continuous canopy with pale, silver-grey foliage.

terrainClasses.label: Forest: Uchkeken, fire-scarred
terrainClasses.paintAs: Burnt and recovering wood: dead grey timber, charred stumps, ash-dark ground, new green returning. Not lush.

terrainClasses.label: Heath and moor
terrainClasses.paintAs: Open upland heath: heather, peat, rough grass, few trees.

terrainClasses.label: Hills and foothills
terrainClasses.paintAs: Rolling hills and the lower slopes of the ranges.

terrainClasses.label: Mountains
terrainClasses.paintAs: Connected rocky mountains with strong relief.

terrainClasses.label: High crests
terrainClasses.paintAs: The highest crests of a range: bare rock, snow only where the manifest marks the range snowy.

geographyGuideLegendBox.note: World rectangle covered by the legend in geography-guide.png. It hides only open lowland.
